audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph ark installation, food distribution, liturgical poem, and ongoing service, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for animal offerings, distribution to women and men, appointed liturgical labor, composite psalm sources, covenant and land language, anointed-leader misuse, interfaith polemic, creation imagery, gathering from nations, daily service, and David's household power.

verses.restored: They brought ark of Divine and set it within tent David pitched for it; they brought burnt offerings and well-being offerings before Divine.
When David finished bringing offerings, he blessed people in name of YHWH.
He distributed to every person of Israel, woman and man, each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat/date cake, and raisin cake.
He appointed some Levites to minister before ark of YHWH, to invoke, thank, and praise YHWH Divine of Israel:
Asaph the chief, second Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with lyres and harps; Asaph sounded cymbals.
Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests sounded trumpets continually before ark of covenant of Divine.
On that day David first assigned this thanksgiving to YHWH into hand of Asaph and relatives:
Give thanks to YHWH; call upon the name; make deeds known among peoples.
Sing to YHWH, make music; speak of all wondrous works.
Boast in holy name; let heart of those seeking YHWH rejoice.
Seek YHWH and strength; seek the face continually.
Remember wondrous works done, signs, and judgments of the mouth,
offspring of Israel servant, children of Jacob chosen ones.
YHWH is our Divine; judgments are in all earth.
Remember covenant continually, word commanded for a thousand generations,
covenant cut with Abraham and oath to Isaac,
established to Jacob as statute and to Israel as enduring covenant,
saying, To you I will give land of Canaan as portion of inheritance,
when you were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.
They walked from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
YHWH permitted no one to oppress them and rebuked kings for their sake,
saying, Do not touch my anointed ones, and do my prophets no harm.
Sing to YHWH, all earth; announce salvation day after day.
Recount glory among nations, wonders among all peoples.
For great is YHWH and greatly praised, and awe-inspiring above all gods.
For all gods of peoples are idols/nothings, but YHWH made heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before YHWH; strength and joy are in the place.
Give to YHWH, families of peoples, give to YHWH glory and strength.
Give to YHWH glory of the name; carry an offering and come before YHWH; bow in splendor of holiness.
Tremble before YHWH, all earth; world is established and shall not totter.
Let heavens rejoice and earth be glad; let them say among nations, YHWH reigns.
Let sea thunder and its fullness; let field rejoice and all within it.
Then trees of forest shall sing before YHWH, for YHWH comes to judge earth.
Give thanks to YHWH, for good; covenant-love endures forever.
Say, Save us, Divine of our salvation; gather and rescue us from nations, to thank holy name and praise.
Blessed is YHWH Divine of Israel from age to age. All people said, Amen, and praised YHWH.
David left Asaph and relatives there before ark of covenant of YHWH to minister continually, according to each day's work.
Also Obed-edom and sixty-eight relatives; Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
Zadok the priest and priestly relatives were before dwelling of YHWH at high place in Gibeon,
to offer burnt offerings to YHWH on altar continually morning and evening, according to all written in Torah YHWH commanded Israel.
With them Heman, Jeduthun, and remaining chosen and named people gave thanks to YHWH, for covenant-love endures forever.
With them Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets, cymbals, and instruments for sacred song; sons of Jeduthun were at gate.
All people went each to their house, and David returned to bless his household.

translation_notes: The celebration includes animal offerings; their lives and the labor of preparing and distributing food should not vanish beneath liturgy.
Food is distributed explicitly to women and men. Equitable nourishment is a material part of public worship.
Verses 8-36 combine material also found in Psalms 105, 96, and 106; liturgical composition and reuse should be acknowledged.
Land-covenant language remembers a small sojourning people and may not authorize modern displacement, annexation, or denial of other peoples' homes.
'Do not touch my anointed ones' addresses vulnerable patriarchs/prophets in the poem and may never establish immunity for kings, clergy, celebrities, or abusive leaders.
Polemic against other gods belongs to ancient Israelite worship and must not support contempt, vandalism, or violence toward living religious communities.
The sea, fields, and trees participate in praise and judgment; ecological communities are not merely resources for royal and temple projects.
The plea to be gathered from nations is a displaced people's prayer, not permission for xenophobia against the nations among whom they live.
Continual worship depends on scheduled labor by musicians, priests, and gatekeepers; daily sacred work requires rest, safety, and material support.
David returns to bless his household, but 2 Samuel 6 preserves conflict with Michal and unequal royal household power that Chronicles omits.
safety_note: Do not weaponize covenant land, 'anointed' status, religious polemic, or gathering language. Center equitable food, ecological praise, displaced people, accountable leaders, interfaith dignity, animal life, and the workers sustaining daily worship.
